OCP extension seam for the upload-preprocessor registry. The file's top-of-module JSDoc explicitly enumerates planned future preprocessors that will extend this registry: 'HEIC: transcode to JPEG (browsers can't display HEIC) — future', 'Animated GIF: extract first frame as poster, set `animated` manifest flag — future', 'JPEG with EXIF: apply orientation, strip personal metadata — future'. The export pairs with `runPreprocessors`'s default-parameter pattern (line 111: `preprocessors: readonly UploadPreprocessor[] = defaultPreprocessors`) — that pattern only makes sense as a named exported registry callers can compose against via `[...defaultPreprocessors, customPreprocessor]`. Two consumers (ingest.ts:100, ingest-locale.ts:90) document the `preprocessors?` input field's default behavior by referencing `defaultPreprocessors` by name in JSDoc. The file's SOLID-lenses section explicitly calls out 'OCP: adding a format = new module + register; ingest unchanged' — the registry IS the registration point. Deleting now and re-introducing when the first future preprocessor lands would force JSDoc churn at three locations + re-promotion of the const. Cost of keeping: one named const.

Load-bearing internal helper for a public-API type. `HasEmbeddedBrand<T>` is used at types.ts:409 by the `Content<T>` type mapper, which IS exported as part of the public `gazetta/schema` surface (re-exported from packages/gazetta/src/schema/index.ts:36 and documented as the canonical usage pattern in its top-of-file JSDoc — template authors write `TemplateFunction<Content<z.infer<typeof schema>>>`). Deleting `HasEmbeddedBrand` would break `Content<T>` and the public schema API; tests in packages/gazetta/tests/schema-content.test.ts cover this composition end-to-end across all three branded asset kinds. The type is also part of a deliberately parallel triad with `HasDownloadableBrand` and `HasFontBrand` (declared on adjacent lines with identical structure, sharing one section comment that frames them as 'Brand detection for Content<T>' and explicitly calls out 'If Zod v5 changes brand representation, update only this module'). The trio forms one coherent brand-detection module — splitting one out would break the parallelism that makes future Zod-version migrations a single localized edit. Knip flagged it because no external file imports it directly, but the internal use by an exported type is what makes it load-bearing.

Knip false positive — the type is used at line 411 in the same module, inside the `Content<T>` type mapper (`: HasDownloadableBrand<T> extends true ? ResolvedDownloadableAsset : ...`). Deleting it would break the type-level `Content<T>` cascade and the build. Knip flagged it as 'unused export' because no OTHER file imports it (the type is only used within its declaration file). The proper resolution is a refactor — drop the `export` keyword from all three brand predicates (`HasEmbeddedBrand`, `HasDownloadableBrand`, `HasFontBrand`) so they become file-scoped — but the per-finding prompt says 'this bot deletes; it doesn't redesign,' so refactor is out of scope. The three types form an intentional coherent triple: the file's own comment block at lines 374-389 explicitly calls them out as a group ('If Zod v5 changes brand representation, update only the `Has*Brand` predicates') and they are exported symmetrically. Maintainer judgment is needed on whether to: (a) drop `export` on all three (most likely correct — they're internal to `Content<T>`'s implementation and not re-exported from `schema/index.ts`), (b) leave as-is (cheap, type-level only, no runtime cost), or (c) promote to public API by adding to `schema/index.ts`'s re-export list (if external type authors writing utilities like `IsAssetRef<T>` would benefit). Note: knip flagged only this one of the triple; if knip is configured to nudge toward file-scoping unused exports, then `HasEmbeddedBrand` and `HasFontBrand` should be flagged too — the asymmetry may itself be a knip quirk. None of the three are in `packages/gazetta/package.json`'s `./schema` exports map (verified — `schema/index.ts` re-exports a curated set that excludes the `Has*Brand` predicates).

Knip is technically correct — no source file imports from the `primeicons` npm package — but the dependency encodes clear intent that needs a human design decision before removal. Evidence of intent: (1) `apps/admin/index.html` line 8 loads the PrimeIcons stylesheet via the unpkg CDN: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/primeicons/primeicons.css">`; (2) the admin uses 131 `pi pi-*` PrimeIcons CSS class references across 35 Vue components (e.g. ComponentTree.vue 12, CmsToolbar.vue 11, AuditDrawer.vue 9, plus PreviewPanel/PublishPanel/DevPlayground/TemplateImpactPanel/ActiveTargetIndicator/PurgeBlockedModal each with 6-7). The dep at `^7.0.0` matches the unpkg CDN's served version; removing it loses the version-intent record (and the current CDN URL is unpinned, which is a separate latent issue). The right resolution is a refactor a human should choose: (a) delete the dep AND commit to CDN-only delivery (probably pinning the CDN URL to a version while at it), or (b) drop the unpkg `<link>` from index.html and add `import 'primeicons/primeicons.css'` in the client entry so the icons ship through Vite + the vite-plugin-pwa precache like the rest of the assets — path (b) is more consistent with the existing precache strategy (which currently misses the icon font + CSS). Either path is correct; neither is a 'bot deletes; doesn't redesign' move. Verified no other source references to `primeicons` exist beyond the CDN `<link>` and package.json/package-lock.json (the knip-parse.test.ts hits are test fixtures, not real consumers).

Transitively-used build dep that knip's static analysis can't trace across workspaces. The `build:admin` script in packages/gazetta runs `vite build -c ../../apps/admin/vite.config.ts ...` from gazetta's cwd; that config file (apps/admin/vite.config.ts:4) imports `@vitejs/plugin-vue` and uses it as the SFC transform plugin. The dep is also declared in apps/admin/package.json's devDependencies, so under npm workspace hoisting it would still resolve from the hoisted root node_modules even if removed here (verified: the dep is hoisted to root node_modules/@vitejs/plugin-vue and packages/gazetta has no local copy). However, the declaration in gazetta deliberately mirrors `vite` itself in the same devDependencies block — both follow the pattern 'every workspace declares the deps its scripts need to run, even if hoisting would resolve them.' Removing only `@vitejs/plugin-vue` (while keeping `vite`) would break that symmetric pattern; removing both is a maintainer judgment call about whether to treat workspace hoisting as load-bearing for gazetta's prepublishOnly script (`npm run build && npm run build:admin`). The 'don't refactor' rule rules out adjusting both deps together as part of dead-code removal. Other references to `@vitejs/plugin-vue` in the repo (apps/admin/vite.config.ts, apps/admin/vitest.config.ts, .storybook/main.ts) resolve from their own locations and are unaffected.

Structural API surface designed for a planned `--format json` flag. The file's own JSDoc on `InfoSection` (line 100-102) explicitly states: 'Decoupling this from the renderer means a future `--format json` consumes the same data structure.' `InfoVariantRow` is one of four sibling row-type interfaces (`InfoSection`, `InfoVariantRow`, `InfoOverrideRow`, `InfoReferenceRow`) that compose the exported `InfoOutput` shape — all exported symmetrically as the building blocks of the future stable structured output. `InfoVariantRow` IS used internally on line 128 (`variants: InfoVariantRow[]` inside the `InfoOutput` interface) and the export is the registration point for the planned future `--format json` consumers. The file is NOT in `packages/gazetta/package.json`'s `exports` map today, so this isn't a `public-api` skip — it's planned-feature scaffolding for an upcoming CLI flag, not a current public surface. Knip flagged only `InfoVariantRow` of the symmetric quartet; if the maintainer ever decides to drop the export defensively, the right move is to drop `export` on all four row types together (symmetric refactor) or to ship `--format json` so the exports earn their keep — neither is in scope for a 'this bot deletes; doesn't redesign' run. Precedent: matches the `defaultPreprocessors` skip-entry pattern (top-of-module JSDoc enumerating planned future use) and the `HasDownloadableBrand` situation (knip flagging one of a symmetric type group whose proper resolution is a maintainer-decided refactor). Cost of keeping: one named interface export, type-level only, no runtime cost. Cost of dropping: re-adding it (and the sibling row types) when `--format json` ships, plus surprising the next reader who finds an asymmetric public/private split across the four row types.

Knip false positive of the same shape as `HasDownloadableBrand` (entry 5): the type is structurally used INSIDE its declaration file but never imported externally. `InfoOverrideRow` is used at line 130 as the element type of `InfoOutput.overrides: InfoOverrideRow[]`, where `InfoOutput` is the public type imported by `assets-cli.ts:21` and consumed by `emitInfo()` (which reads `info.overrides[i].selector` and `info.overrides[i].bytes`). Tests in `packages/gazetta/tests/cli-assets-display.test.ts` exercise the field shape at lines 196-199. Three sibling types in the same file follow the EXACT same pattern — `InfoSection` (line 103, used as `metadata: InfoSection`), `InfoVariantRow` (line 108, used as `variants: InfoVariantRow[]`), `InfoReferenceRow` (line 119, used as `references: InfoReferenceRow[]`) — all four exported, all four used only as `InfoOutput` field types within the same file, none imported externally. Knip flagged only `InfoOverrideRow`; the asymmetry mirrors the `Has*Brand` triple where knip flagged one of three with identical usage. The proper resolution is a refactor — either drop the `export` keyword from all four sibling row types (making them internal helpers to `InfoOutput`'s shape declaration) or accept that all four form a symmetric exported sub-shape API alongside the parent `InfoOutput` type. Unilaterally dropping the `export` from only `InfoOverrideRow` would break the deliberate parallel structure (4 sibling types declared back-to-back at lines 103-122, each two/three lines, all exported, each named as the element type of a single `InfoOutput` field) and create a 'why is this one different?' question for future readers. Verified the file is not in `packages/gazetta/package.json`'s `exports` map — it's an internal CLI module, so none of the four sibling row types are public API today. The per-finding prompt's 'this bot deletes; it doesn't redesign' rule excludes the consistent refactor. Cost of keeping: one `export` keyword the symbol-table grep occasionally crosses.

Scaffolding for a planned but not-yet-wired `gazetta/transforms` subpath export. The file's own top-of-module JSDoc (lines 9-11) explicitly documents the intent: 'Operator-facing factories (`sharpAdapter`, `cloudflareAdapter`) live in `factories.ts` and are re-exported below for the `gazetta/transforms` subpath.' That subpath is NOT currently in `packages/gazetta/package.json`'s `exports` map (verified — the map lists `.`, `./types`, `./format`, `./save-etag`, `./editor`, `./admin-api`, `./admin-api/schemas`, `./schema`, `./testing`, `./providers/azure-blob`, `./providers/s3`, `./workers/cloudflare-r2` but has no `./transforms` entry), so the re-export exists as a marker for a planned surface, not a live one. The symbol `cloudflareAdapter` IS load-bearing public API via a DIFFERENT re-export path: `packages/gazetta/src/index.ts:116` (`export { sharpAdapter, cloudflareAdapter } from './transforms/factories.js'`) imports directly from `./transforms/factories.js` (not from this barrel), so operators consuming the `gazetta` package's main entry point are unaffected. Knip is technically correct that no internal caller imports `cloudflareAdapter` from `./transforms/index.js` — internal consumers use `./transforms/factories.js` directly and external consumers use the main `gazetta` re-export. But knip flagged only `cloudflareAdapter` and NOT `sharpAdapter` from the same `export { sharpAdapter, cloudflareAdapter } from './factories.js'` line on line 20 (both symbols share the same import-target reasoning); asymmetrically removing one would break the deliberate parallel structure the file's header comment establishes. Precedent: matches `defaultPreprocessors` (entry 3) and `InfoVariantRow` (entry 9) — top-of-module JSDoc enumerating planned or reserved future use as the intent marker; also matches the `Has*Brand` triple pattern where knip flags one member of a symmetric group whose proper resolution is a maintainer-decided refactor (either wire up the `./transforms` subpath in package.json's exports map + add tests confirming subpath resolution, or drop both the `sharpAdapter` and `cloudflareAdapter` re-exports from this barrel together with a doc-comment update).
